recommendation.recommendation: Conduct a focused field inspection and improve soil organic matter.
recommendation.justification: Current weather, soil pH, nitrogen levels, and canopy vigor are optimal for mango growth, but low soil organic carbon and high surface exposure increase risk of nutrient deficiency and erosion during the critical fruiting stage. Immediate scouting will detect any disease or deficiency, and adding compost will raise organic carbon, improve water retention, and mitigate erosion.
actions: 1. Perform a thorough field inspection to identify signs of anthracnose, powdery mildew, fruit fly, mealybug, or nutrient deficiencies.
2. Record observations and map any problem areas.
3. Apply well‑decomposed compost or organic manure uniformly across the orchard at a rate of 5 t ha⁻¹ (or 2 kg m⁻²) to raise organic carbon.
4. Incorporate the organic material into the top 15 cm of soil using light tillage or a rotavator.
5. Re‑water using existing drip irrigation schedule (every 7–10 days) to aid incorporation.
recommendation.expected_outcome: Enhanced soil organic carbon will improve nutrient availability and water retention, reducing yield risk during fruiting. Early disease detection and treatment will protect canopy health, maintaining the high NDVI and supporting profitable harvests.
monitoring_plan: • Weekly visual scouting for disease symptoms and pest activity for the next 4 weeks.
• Soil organic carbon test 30 days after compost application to verify improvement.
• Re‑capture satellite NDVI/NDWI data (or drone imagery) after 2 weeks to confirm canopy vigor remains high.
• Record any erosion signs after rain events and adjust mulching if needed.

actions: 1. Perform a thorough field inspection to identify signs of anthracnose, powdery mildew, fruit fly, mealybug, or nutrient deficiencies.
2. Record observations and map any problem areas.
3. Apply well‑decomposed compost or organic manure uniformly across the orchard at a rate of 5 t ha⁻¹ (or 2 kg m⁻²) to raise organic carbon.
4. Incorporate the organic material into the top 15 cm of soil using light tillage or a rotavator.
5. Re‑water using existing drip irrigation schedule (every 7–10 days) to aid incorporation.
steps.justification: Current weather, soil pH, nitrogen levels, and canopy vigor are optimal for mango growth, but low soil organic carbon and high surface exposure increase risk of nutrient deficiency and erosion during the critical fruiting stage.
